title: Volume of Prisms and Surface Area
kicker: Cambridge Lower Secondary · Mathematics 0862 · Stage 8 · Geometry and Measure
summary: Derive and use the formula for the volume of a triangular prism, and calculate the surface area of cubes, cuboids, triangular prisms and pyramids.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Use what you know about area and the volume of a cuboid to explain (derive) the formula for the volume of a triangular prism, and use the formula to calculate volumes of triangular prisms. [8Gg.06]
Use area and the properties of cubes, cuboids, triangular prisms and pyramids to calculate their surface area. [8Gg.08]

blocks.text: **Volume** tells you how much space a solid takes up (how many 1 cm cubes would fill it). **Surface area** tells you the total area of all the faces on the outside (how much paper you would need to wrap it with no overlaps). They are different ideas with different units: volume is measured in **cubic units** (cm³, m³) and surface area in **square units** (cm², m²). On this page you will build the volume formula for a triangular prism from the cuboid, and then learn a reliable method for the surface area of any cube, cuboid, triangular prism or pyramid.
1. Key words

items: volume
الحجم — the amount of space inside a 3D shape, in cm³ or m³
surface area
المساحة الكلية (مساحة السطح) — the total area of all the faces, in cm² or m²
prism
منشور — a solid with the same cross-section all the way along its length
cross-section
المقطع العرضي — the shape you see when you cut straight across a prism
triangular prism
منشور ثلاثي — a prism whose cross-section is a triangle (5 faces: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles)
cuboid
متوازي المستطيلات — a prism with 6 rectangular faces
cube
مكعب — a cuboid whose 6 faces are equal squares
pyramid
هرم — a solid with a flat base and triangular faces that meet at one point (the apex)
apex
الرأس — the top point of a pyramid
face / edge / vertex
وجه / حرف / رأس — flat surface / line where two faces meet / corner
net
شبكة المجسم (المفكوك) — a flat shape that folds up to make the solid
perpendicular height
الارتفاع العمودي — the height measured at 90° to the base
slant height
الارتفاع الجانبي (المائل) — the height of a sloping triangular face of a pyramid

blocks.text: 2. Volume of a cuboid — the starting point
A cuboid that is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high holds 5 × 3 = 15 cubes in its bottom layer, and there are 2 layers, so its volume is 15 × 2 = **30 cm³**. In general:

items: **Volume of a cuboid = length × width × height**

The bottom layer (5 × 3 = 15 cm²) is the **area of the cross-section**, and the height (2 cm) is how far that cross-section runs. So we can also say: **volume of a cuboid = area of cross-section × length**.
Volume of a cube with edge a = a × a × a = a³.

blocks.text: 3. Deriving the volume of a triangular prism

Take a cuboid with base b, height h and length l. Cut it straight through from one edge to the opposite edge (along the diagonals of the two end faces). You get **two identical right-angled triangular prisms**, so each one has exactly **half** the volume of the cuboid.

blocks.caption: Cutting a cuboid along the diagonals of its end faces makes two identical triangular prisms.

items: Volume of the cuboid = b × h × l.
Volume of one triangular prism = ½ × b × h × l.
But ½ × b × h is the **area of the triangle** at the end (the cross-section).
So: **volume of a triangular prism = area of the triangular cross-section × length = ½ × b × h × l**.

blocks.text: This also works when the triangle is not right-angled: any triangle with base b and perpendicular height h has area ½ × b × h (you met this when you found the area of a triangle as half of a rectangle). The prism is just that triangle 'pushed along' a length l. The rule **volume = area of cross-section × length** works for **every prism**: cube, cuboid, triangular prism, and later prisms with other cross-sections.

blocks.title: Which 'height'?
blocks.text: A triangular prism has two different lengths that students mix up: the **height of the triangle** (used to find the triangle's area) and the **length of the prism** (how far the triangle is pushed back). First find the triangle's area, then multiply by the length. Always use the **perpendicular** height of the triangle — never a sloping side.

blocks.title: القاعدة اللي لازم تحفظها
items: حجم المنشور الثلاثي = مساحة المثلث (المقطع العرضي) × طول المنشور.
مساحة المثلث = ½ × القاعدة × الارتفاع العمودي.
المنشور الثلاثي هو نص متوازي مستطيلات، علشان كده فيه ½.
الحجم وحدته cm³ (تكعيب)، والمساحة وحدتها cm² (تربيع).

blocks.text: 4. Surface area — add up every face
To find a surface area, imagine **unfolding the solid into its net**. The surface area is the total area of the net. Work face by face and list the faces so you do not miss one.

rows: 3 pairs of equal rectangles: top & bottom, front & back, two ends
2 equal triangles + 3 rectangles (one for each side of the triangle)
4 triangles (the base is a triangle too)

blocks.text: **A neat trick for triangular prisms:** the three rectangles all have the same length l, and their widths are the three sides of the triangle. So the three rectangles together = **perimeter of the triangle × length**.

blocks.text: For a **pyramid**, the triangular faces slope. The height you need for each triangle is its **slant height** (from the apex down the middle of the face to the base edge), not the vertical height of the pyramid.

blocks.text: **Method for any surface-area question**

items: Name the solid and count its faces (cube 6, cuboid 6, triangular prism 5, square-based pyramid 5).
Sketch the net or list the faces in groups of equal faces.
Find the area of each different face (rectangle = l × w, triangle = ½ × b × h).
Multiply by how many of each face there are, and add.
Check you have the right number of faces, and write the answer in **square units**.

blocks.title: فرق مهم
blocks.text: الحجم = المساحة اللي جوه المجسم (cm³). المساحة الكلية = مجموع مساحات كل الأوجه من بره (cm²). في المساحة الكلية: افرد المجسم (الشبكة) واجمع مساحة كل وجه — وماتنساش ولا وجه!
5. Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — The triangular prism in the diagram above has a triangle with base 6 cm and height 4 cm, and length 10 cm. Work out its volume. [2]

items: Area of the triangle = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm².
Volume = area of cross-section × length = 12 × 10 = **120 cm³**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: 6 × 4 × 10 = 240 cm³ — this forgets the ½ and gives the volume of the whole cuboid.
**Worked example 2** — A triangular prism has volume 180 cm³. Its cross-section is a triangle with base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. Find the length of the prism. Show your working. [2]

items: Area of the triangle = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm².
Volume = area × length, so 180 = 20 × length.

blocks.text: **Worked example 3** — Find the surface area of a cuboid 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high. [2]
Common mistake: adding 15 + 10 + 6 = 31 cm² and forgetting that each face has an equal opposite face. Compare: its volume is 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cm³ — a different number and a different unit.

**Worked example 4** — The net above belongs to a triangular prism with a right-angled triangle of sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm and length 10 cm. Work out (a) its surface area [2] and (b) its volume. [1]

items: (a) Two triangles: 2 × (½ × 3 × 4) = 2 × 6 = 12 cm². (The right angle is between the 3 cm and 4 cm sides, so these are the base and height.)
Three rectangles: 3 × 10 + 4 × 10 + 5 × 10 = 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 cm² (or perimeter × length = 12 × 10 = 120 cm²).
Surface area = 12 + 120 = **132 cm²**.
(b) Volume = 6 × 10 = **60 cm³**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: using the 5 cm side as the height of the triangle. The 5 cm side is the sloping side (hypotenuse); the base and perpendicular height are 3 cm and 4 cm.
**Worked example 5** — A square-based pyramid has a base of side 6 cm. Each triangular face has a slant height of 5 cm. Work out the total surface area. [2]

items: Base: 6 × 6 = 36 cm².
One triangle: ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 cm². Four triangles: 4 × 15 = 60 cm².
Surface area = 36 + 60 = **96 cm²**.

blocks.text: **Worked example 6 (thinking mathematically)** — A cube has a surface area of 150 cm². Work out its volume. [2]

items: A cube has 6 equal square faces, so one face = 150 ÷ 6 = 25 cm².
Each edge = √25 = 5 cm.

blocks.text: Common mistake: dividing 150 by 6 and then cubing 25. You must find the **edge** first (the square root of the face area).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Forgetting the ½ for the triangle (this doubles the prism's volume).
Using a sloping side instead of the perpendicular height of the triangle.
Counting only one of the two triangular ends, or only one of each pair of rectangles on a cuboid.
Using the vertical height of a pyramid instead of the slant height of its triangular faces.
Wrong units: volume must be cm³ (or m³), surface area cm² (or m²).
Mixing units: if one length is in metres and the others in centimetres, change them all to the same unit first.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: A labelled diagram marked NOT TO SCALE with an answer line and the unit printed after it — read every measurement carefully and decide which ones you need.
'Show your working' — write the area of the cross-section first, then the multiplication. Method marks are given for working even if the final answer is wrong.
Working backwards: the volume or surface area is given and you find a missing length.

Real contexts: a tent, a ramp, a chocolate box, a water trough. Decide whether the question wants space inside (volume) or material on the outside (surface area) — and whether a face is missing (an open box, a tent with no floor).
Explain or critique: 'Ali says the volume doubles when … Is he correct? Explain.' Give a calculation as evidence.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Volume of Prisms and Surface Area — practice
blocks.intro: 13 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. You may use a calculator. Write units and show your working on paper; open answers are self-marked with the mark scheme.

questions.q: Which of these always gives the volume of a triangular prism?
c: base × height × length of the triangle's sides
area of the triangular cross-section × length
questions.e: Every prism: volume = area of cross-section × length. For a triangular prism the cross-section is the triangle, so V = (½ × b × h) × l. Perimeter × length gives the area of the three rectangles (part of the surface area), not the volume.

questions.q: A triangular prism has a cross-section of area 15 cm² and a length of 8 cm. Work out its volume.
questions.e: Volume = area of cross-section × length = 15 × 8 = 120 cm³.

questions.q: Work out the volume of this triangular prism. The triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. The prism is 12 cm long.
questions.e: Area of triangle = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². Volume = 30 × 12 = 360 cm³. (1 mark for 30 seen, or for ½ × 10 × 6 × 12.)

questions.q: Work out the surface area of a cube with edges of 4 cm.
questions.e: One face = 4 × 4 = 16 cm². A cube has 6 faces: 6 × 16 = 96 cm².

questions.q: A cuboid measures 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm. Work out its surface area.
questions.e: 8 × 5 = 40, 8 × 3 = 24, 5 × 3 = 15. Each pair: 2 × (40 + 24 + 15) = 2 × 79 = 158 cm². (1 mark for the three different face areas or for 79.)

questions.q: A triangular prism has volume 252 cm³. Its cross-section is a triangle with base 7 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Work out the length of the prism.
questions.e: Area of triangle = ½ × 7 × 6 = 21 cm². Length = 252 ÷ 21 = 12 cm. Check: 21 × 12 = 252 ✓

questions.q: The prism has a right-angled triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Its length is 15 cm. Work out its total surface area.
questions.e: Two triangles: 2 × (½ × 6 × 8) = 2 × 24 = 48 cm². Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 15 = 24 × 15 = 360 cm². Total = 48 + 360 = 408 cm². (1 mark triangles 48 or 24 seen; 1 mark rectangles 360 or any two of 90, 120, 150; 1 mark answer.)

questions.q: A square-based pyramid has a base of side 10 cm. Each triangular face has a slant height of 12 cm. Work out its total surface area.
questions.e: Base = 10 × 10 = 100 cm². One triangle = ½ × 10 × 12 = 60 cm²; four triangles = 240 cm². Total = 100 + 240 = 340 cm².

questions.q: A cube has a surface area of 54 cm². What is its volume?
questions.e: One face = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 cm², so the edge = √9 = 3 cm. Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm³. (729 = 9³ comes from cubing the face area — a common mistake.)

questions.p: A tent is a triangular prism. It has two triangular ends and two sloping rectangular sides. It has no floor.

questions.q: The ends are triangles with base 1.6 m and height 0.6 m. Each sloping side is 1 m wide and 2 m long. Work out the area of material needed to make the tent.
questions.e: One triangle = ½ × 1.6 × 0.6 = 0.48 m²; two ends = 0.96 m². One sloping side = 1 × 2 = 2 m²; two sides = 4 m². There is no floor, so do not add the 1.6 × 2 rectangle. Total = 0.96 + 4 = 4.96 m².

questions.q: A wooden beam is a prism 1.2 m long. Its cross-section has an area of 50 cm². Work out its volume in cm³.
questions.e: Change the length to centimetres first: 1.2 m = 120 cm. Volume = 50 × 120 = 6000 cm³. (50 × 1.2 = 60 mixes units and scores 0.)

questions.q: Sami says: 'If you double the length of a triangular prism, its volume doubles.' Huda says: 'If you double both the base and the height of the triangle, the volume doubles too.' Who is correct? Explain your answer.
questions.ms: 1 mark: Sami is correct, with a reason, e.g. V = area × length, so 2 × length gives 2 × V (or a numerical example). 1 mark: Huda is not correct, with a reason, e.g. the triangle's area becomes ½ × 2b × 2h = 4 × ½bh, so the volume is multiplied by 4 (or a numerical example such as b = 2, h = 2, l = 5: 10 cm³ becomes 40 cm³). Do not accept 'Huda is wrong' with no reason.
questions.e: Volume = ½ × b × h × l. Doubling l: ½ × b × h × 2l = 2 × (½bhl) — the volume doubles, so Sami is right. Doubling b and h: ½ × 2b × 2h × l = 4 × (½bhl) — the volume is four times as big, so Huda is wrong. Example: b = 4, h = 3, l = 10 gives 60 cm³; with b = 8, h = 6 it gives 240 cm³ = 4 × 60.

questions.q: Omar works out the surface area of the prism in question 7 like this: ½ × 6 × 8 + 6 × 15 + 8 × 15 + 10 × 15 = 384 cm². Explain the mistake Omar made and write the correct surface area.
questions.ms: 1 mark: he has only included one triangle / forgot the second triangular end (accept: he needs to add another 24 cm²). 1 mark: correct answer 408 cm².
questions.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. Omar counted only one triangle (24 cm²). Correct total = 384 + 24 = 408 cm².

blocks.title: Remember
items: Volume of any prism = area of cross-section × length; for a triangular prism V = ½ × b × h × l (half a cuboid).
Use the perpendicular height of the triangle, not a sloping side.
Surface area = total area of all the faces (think of the net): cube 6a², cuboid 2(lw + lh + wh).
Triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles (perimeter × length). Square-based pyramid: base² + 4 triangles using the slant height.
Units: volume in cm³ or m³, surface area in cm² or m² — and make all lengths the same unit first.
